checked_hypothesis_notes: The smooth-conformal regularity argument needs complex dimension at least two.
The isolated-puncture upper bound uses two independent coordinate discs and dimension at least two.
Uniform exponential integrability uses a positive Hermitian background, normalized L1 compactness and qualitative Skoda; no bounded mass assumption.
The Cegrell carrier assertion is a stated external local decomposition; the disk carrier is proved by exponential damping.
Planar inverse maximum uses the bounded distributional/canonical limit of capacitary functions; their pointwise values on a polar set need not converge to that representative.
The polar maximum identity is proved after a common smooth correction, retaining positivity when subtracting the shared polar measure.
Mixed nonclosed-product positivity is proved by coefficient freezing and closed Hessians, not by positivity of signed expansion terms.
Submersion pullback commutes with bounded products; products beyond the base dimension vanish by degree.
Continuous-density coefficient recovery uses a smooth radial approximate identity, Minkowski convolution, differentiation of measures and Fatou.
The convex-pair C11 weight conclusion asserts positivity and the product inequality; it does not claim the smooth second-derivative identity for a nonsmooth weight.
Global capacity controls tests with a fixed bounded range; this does not impose ambient bounded mass over all bounded potentials.
Uniform capacity absolute continuity requires a finite non-pluripolar measure.
Curve zero-area collapse needs only uniform background convergence: total variation of curvature and L1 compactness give uniform capacity convergence.
Exact bounded smooth regularization is asserted only in the positive Hermitian background omega; general smooth theta keeps a vanishing curvature error.
The smooth-maximum diagonal uses a uniform positive margin above the original bounded potential and compact decreasing level sets; it does not assume the potential is continuous.
The disc multiplier ideal is generated by z to floor(lambda), including the strict integer borderline and the separately defined zero coefficient.
Analytic restriction requires a presentation ideal not identically zero on the submanifold; zero generic Lelong number alone does not make an arbitrary restriction genuine.
Submersion pullback commutes with each multiplier ideal; under modifications the adjoint transform retains the Jacobian, while ideal order at all weights is birationally invariant.

The general Chern regularization input initially has only a vanishing modulus. Its separate smooth-background linear-rate argument uses the higher-order classical expansion and normalized trace-mass bounds; that expansion remains an external dependency, not an independently reproved theorem.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Optimal damping rate on the Hopf threefold
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_text: The optimal damping rate remains undetermined here.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Exponential subsolutions at zero individual threshold
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: The next estimate quantifies this scalar error when the density root is approximable by bounded roots. Whether an exponential subsolution exists when $b_h(f)=0$ is a separate question; \cref{thm:individual-exponential-subsolution} applies whenever such a subsolution is available.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Exact individual normalized equation at the attained threshold
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: The distinction is caused by the order restriction on a smooth test: it cannot use a measurable increase of a density whose essential lower value is unchanged in every open set. Bounded measurable tests retain this information. The theorem concerns subsolution existence for individual $L^1$ densities. A characterization of exact normalized equations at $b_h(f)$, including their natural singularity class and finite-mass compactness, remains a separate problem.
additional_open_remarks_encountered.inventory_relationship: Expository occurrence of the existing formal problem, not a new formal question

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Equality of the bounded-root closure and admissible root space when lower mass vanishes
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: The same tail estimate gives a uniform exponential-damping modulus and scalar error bounds in \cref{prop:exponential-root-tail-modulus}. It does not, by itself, give capacity convergence of equation potentials. When lower mass vanishes, equality of $\mathcal D_h^0$ and $\mathcal D_h$ remains a separate question.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Uniqueness of supporting probabilities at continuous Hermitian and general singular-reference densities
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: Thus for a continuous $F$ in the Hermitian case, smooth approximations $F_j\to F$ uniformly produce Gauduchon adjoint probabilities whose weak cluster points all belong to $\mathcal A_0(F)$ and are absolutely continuous. If $\mathcal A_0(F)$ is a singleton, the weak limit is independent of this approximation. In particular this holds at every $F\in\mathscr U_0$. Uniqueness at every continuous density remains unresolved in this Hermitian setting, and likewise for the general singular references considered above.
additional_open_remarks_encountered.inventory_relationship: The Hermitian zero-reference clause is an expository occurrence of conjecture conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint; the general singular-reference extension is broader. No new numbered problem or equivalence is claimed.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Weak cofactor-current identification and compatibility with approximation
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: A weak linearized operator requires more than a supporting probability. In this Hermitian zero-reference setting, \cref{thm:gaud-current-all-adjoints} represents each supporting probability by a determinant-weighted positive $\ddc$-closed current. Identifying that current with a scalar multiple of the weak power $\omega_u^{n-1}$ requires a justified product and compatibility with approximation.
additional_open_remarks_encountered.inventory_relationship: An explicit unresolved product/approximation requirement in this chapter, not a separately numbered conjecture. No assertion that every restricted case is open in the literature.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: For ordinary divisorial types, a relative comparison of positive residual forms supplies a geometric criterion for this functional convergence, as proved next. General convergence criteria for references with degenerate residuals or arbitrary singularities remain open.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Unrestricted reverse inclusion from zero-obstacle equality to all-obstacle equality
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: The inclusion $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{all}}_\omega\subseteq\mathcal G_\omega$ follows by taking $F=0$. For $q=P_\omega[u]_{\mathcal I}$, \cref{prop:ideal-obstacle-reprojection} reduces the reverse inclusion to $P_{\omega,F}[u]=P_{\omega,F}[q]$ for every $F$. Membership in $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,\omega,q)$ suffices. Under bounded mass and positive lower volume of $q$, this membership is equivalent to zero-obstacle equality, by \cref{prop:conditional-i-characterization}. On curves the two closure sets coincide even at zero mass, by \cref{prop:curve-all-obstacle-topology}. The relative-divisor reduction below gives higher-dimensional zero-volume cases over curves. A separate example has a base potential in the required relative envelope class and an ambient background with unbounded mass. The unrestricted implication remains unresolved here. Although $\tau^{\mathrm{all}}_\omega$ removes the fixed-obstacle gauge dependence, it still has incomplete curve families and remains strictly weaker than polar total variation on ordinary curve models, by \cref{prop:curve-all-obstacle-incomplete}.
additional_open_remarks_encountered.inventory_relationship: A separate unresolved implication; the retained bounded-mass/positive-lower-volume and specified product results do not establish it. Related to the topology program, without claiming equivalence to its formal metric problem.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Complete topology with analytic closure and background compatibility
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: Changing the curve areas rescales the polar distances, and a zero area removes its metric coordinate. The comparisons in \cref{prop:weighted-product-metric-comparison} quantify this change even when the active coordinates differ. If the curve backgrounds converge uniformly to zero-area forms, the diameters vanish and the potentials converge in $L^1$, uniformly over the model tuples. Their limit still contains the normalized smooth potentials of the limiting backgrounds, by \cref{cor:arbitrary-product-zero-area-collapse}. Thus these loci describe concrete degenerations beyond the positive-volume theory. Extending the complete topology to general ordinary models, while retaining analytic closure and compatibility across backgrounds, remains open.

additional_open_remarks_encountered.topic: Relation of Perron interpolation to a complete metric on Hermitian singularity classes
additional_open_remarks_encountered.exact_source_line: The three-dimensional torus in \cref{ex:gauduchon-persistence-torus} carries a Gauduchon form $\omega$ and a smooth potential $u\in\HH_\omega$ for which $\omega_u$ is not Gauduchon. Thus $u_t=u+t$ is a smooth Perron segment that is not stationary for the $L^2$ action. On a surface, the Gauduchon condition persists under potential perturbations by \cref{prop:gauduchon-potential-persistence}, but it does not cancel the first-derivative terms in \eqref{eq:hermitian-ltwo-geodesic}. Relating Perron interpolation to a complete metric on Hermitian singularity classes remains a separate problem.
